Pluralistic approaches to morality can provide insights into the “why” and “how” of variation in different moral-psychological outcomes over historical time and across different regions. In this article, we review recent developments in the study of morality from a pluralistic approach across time and space. We review the emerging research in the historical psychology of morality and call for the expansion of the remit of moral psychology from an individual-focused approach to the study of norms and values in collectives, both in different populations and different historical eras. ## Restore content access. * 48 hours access to article PDF & online version. * Article PDF can be downloaded. * Article PDF can be printed.
